## SMP6 · SMP6-zeroing-billed-to-nobody — R81 zeroing whose payer was destroyed meanwhile is billed to nobody: a stated exception to R10's 'no part of a destruction is billed to nobody', or bill it elsewhere?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 14

On behalf of: Implementer

Evidence: Rulings applied on wp-SMP6 8fb11dc37 + 938a92b17 (base 98b866854): a dying budget's pending zeroing debt is lifted at destruction to R10's payer (payer tables rewritten under the lock; root's to nobody as one clause); (A) no zeroing at an exit, idle harts drain, an allocation finding the bitmap empty takes one frame from any hart's pending list under the lock (the implementer's form, accepted over the want-IPI clause; pending lists written only under the lock, no store-backs; the destruction audit counts in-flight frames); orchestrator's A1/A3 for icount's shared clock recorded in architect-questions.md 'SMP6 A1/A3' with the residual on memory.md. Measured and stated on memory.md: no saving on the containment gate, ~79.5k frames in flight to the run's end, a busy hart keeps allocations at main's cost. kernel-red OK at 8fb11dc37; model-mutations caught; smp-inflight-race under memory pressure both widths.

Event: `aa6f0a8ac0cb14d92135f19403bef41a` · 2026-10-09T20:08:31Z

> From smp6-implementer-2 (non-blocking; it runs its gates meanwhile and will write R10 as a stated exception plus a residual unless you rule otherwise). SMP6 (wp-SMP6, worktree .worktrees/SMP6, design .wash/local/SMP6-design.md): a freed frame is zeroed by the freeing hart after it releases the lock; the zeroing is billed at the hart's next entry to the budgets paying when the frames were freed (the caller, a destroyer, a deadline's payer), recorded as `z` (sched::bill_zeroing). When that payer was itself destroyed in between, the code bills the zeroing to nobody. docs/kernel/budgets.md R10 says 'no part of a destruction is billed to nobody' and says nothing of zeroing. Options: (a) R10 gains a stated exception: zeroing after the payer's own destruction is billed to nobody, bounded by the frames one section can free (64 staged per hart plus the pending list), with the residual stated; (b) bill it to the destroyed budget's parent (the one that pays destruction's remainder under R10 today, if that is how R10 handles a dying subtree's costs), which keeps R10's sentence true; (c) bill it to the destroyer (the budget whose call destroyed the payer). Please weigh against B24's per-case 'nobody N of 1000' measurement (the oracle reports the share of kernel time billed to no budget; an exception raises it in destruction-heavy cases such as kernel-containment and sched-exit-churn) and against R10's cost bound (would (b) or (c) need a lookup the hart cannot make without the lock?). Answer on this thread; the implementer reads it.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `2dbfcca5041d41aed277ccafd6ae7eb2` · 2026-10-09T20:10:20Z

> Ruling: none of (a), (b), (c) as posed. A dying budget's pending zeroing debt is lifted with the rest of its debt at the destruction, not looked up at the bill. Full note: .wash/local/architect-questions.md, SMP6.
> 
> Mechanism: the destruction, under the lock, between `mark_dying` and the free, walks every hart's zeroing-payer table (`MAX_HARTS x ZEROING_PAYERS` = 4 entries each) and rewrites each entry naming a dying budget to the destruction's R10 payer: the caller for `budget_destroy`/`budget_reap`; for a deadline the parent after the carve returns, or the nearest ancestor with free weight above 0, which R10 names at step 1 anyway. The table is written at release and read at the next acquisition, both under the lock, so the destroyer sees every pending entry and no hart looks anything up outside the lock. Cost: a constant number of entries, one dying-flag read each: inside R10's bound. `is_live_budget` at the bill becomes a debug assertion. A payer destroyed on this hart by the entry's expiry is covered by order: expiry rewrites, then the bill.
> 
> Why: (a) raises B24's nobody share in exactly the destruction-heavy cases and adds a residual for a cost we can name a payer for; (b) and (c) need, at bill time, a parent or destroyer of a budget whose frame is gone, which nothing records. The lift is what R10 and scheduling.md:364 already do with a dying budget's remainder. R10's sentence stays true as written.
> 
> The one exception: `root`'s destruction has no successor; its entries go to nobody, with nothing left to run. One clause in R10's billing paragraph, not a residual.
> 
> Conditions: scheduling.md's `z` text says the lift; deadline-flood-billed's nobody N of 1000 shows no rise from zeroing at 2 harts; a check that a destruction rewrites a pending entry (mutation or unit test).
> 
> Side finding for the same edit: budgets.md:332-335 ("the kernel departs from this ... to nobody") contradicts R10 at :639-644 and cites a residual that is gone. Remove it while R10 is open.

That hart takes no device or timer interrupt for 120 ms; at one hart that is the machine. Event: `b5f28eaae83aa9a7c86f3ac658be8ec1` · 2026-10-09T21:34:38Z

> Ruling: the quota form, amended for idle. Note: architect-questions.md, "SMP6 zeroing quota".
> 
> A hart zeroes at most 64 pending frames per kernel exit: about 2 ms under icount, inside the one-section bound every interrupt already waits behind, so no new latency class. The idle loop zeroes the same 64 per pass and returns to its interrupt-enabled top between passes, so an idle hart drains promptly and still answers an interrupt within 2 ms; without this the idle drain is the 120 ms again. The rest stay in flight and drain on later exits, on idle, and under the lock one at a time when an allocation finds the bitmap empty (the design's existing rule, so memory availability holds at one hart too). R81 and the in-flight invariant are unchanged; the pending set is bounded by RAM.
> 
> Why not interrupts enabled between frames: a trap taken in kernel mode over a committed pick is a new trap origin, with the pick abandoned or resumed; that is a bigger mechanism than a counter (Tenet 1). Keep it in the design file as the alternative if the drain proves too slow.
> 
> Conditions:
> 1. The bill per exit is proportional to the frames zeroed that exit, the payer table carrying across exits (entries decrement as their frames zero; the lift rule from the earlier ruling applies to what remains).
> 2. The lease-destruction gate records, after the change, the longest interrupts-off stretch and the exits taken to drain the ~4270 frames; both go on the page.
> 3. memory.md states the quota, the drain, and that a destroyer's caller sees R10's walk, not the zeroing; kernel-red's P2-3 residual takes the new number.
> 4. One constant, its reason (the section bound) beside it.

Event: `ec23f99597451a577e5d265946f4280c` · 2026-10-09T22:26:24Z

> Ruling: (A), with your four conditions and one hole closed. Note: architect-questions.md, SMP6, "Superseded".
> 
> (A) is main's cost under load and free when idle: an allocation that finds the bitmap empty zeroes one frame under the lock, as every allocation did on main, billed as the allocation's own kernel time; idle time drains 64 per pass. Nobody who did not free pays at an exit, so the notice path returns to main's. (B) still taxes the next runner for another's frees; (C) is the most mechanism for the same result.
> 
> The hole: with exits zeroing nothing, a hart's pending frames drain only when that hart idles or allocates. Hart 0 frees 4270 frames, then runs a spinner; hart 1's allocations find the bitmap empty, have no pending of their own, and would wait on hart 0's `done` push that never comes. Close it with the design's `want` flag: the waiting allocator sets `want` and sends the IPI; the owner hart's entry for that IPI zeroes up to 64 before it returns. So "an exit zeroes nothing" reads "unless another hart asked", bounded by the quota, and an allocation waits at most one frame's zeroing (the owner pushes `done` per frame). State it on the page with the other two drains.
> 
> Conditions, yours plus: the on-demand path is one frame per allocation under the lock, no worse than main; the gate records the pending set's high-water mark and the longest time a frame stayed in flight under load; payer table and lift rules unchanged for idle and the wanted exit; P2-3's residual becomes "zeroing runs on idle harts, on demand, and at an exit another hart asked for". The nobody-share rise (rv64 23->29, rv32 34->44 of 1000) is traced before merge: it is the measure the earlier ruling said must not move.

Event: `f5ee97256c20421b64d4f3bb3ea2c36d` · 2026-10-09T22:30:19Z

> SMP6, on (A)'s hole: it is closed already, without the want-IPI exit. Since the quota change, an allocation that finds the bitmap empty takes one pending frame from any hart's list, its own first, under the lock (reclaim::pop_pending), and zeroes it there. That is one frame per allocation, billed as the allocation's own kernel time; the owner's payer table is decremented, unbilled.
> This is safe because a pending list is only ever taken whole. Its owner, idle, swaps it out to zero up to 64 frames and stores back the rest. The lock holder swaps it out to take one frame and stores back the rest. Only the lock holder adds to a list. So in your scenario hart 1 takes hart 0's frame directly; it waits (wait_done) only while hart 0 is zeroing its list, idle, and hart 0 pushes done per frame, so the wait is at most one frame. No hart then zeroes at an exit, not even when asked, which keeps the notice path at main's. The page states the two drains (idle, on demand) and why nothing runs at an exit. If you want the want-IPI exit instead, say so and I will build it. Built and amended (head after this message); the gates and the high-water and longest-in-flight measurements are next, and the nobody-share trace before merge.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `18d2fe8f8885022644712c02dd069fed` · 2026-10-09T22:32:09Z

> No objection: the implementer's form supersedes the want-IPI clause. Less mechanism, same bound.
> 
> One condition on "lists are only ever taken whole". The store-back is where it leaks: the idle owner stores its remainder back outside the lock, and the lock holder stores back the rest after taking one; a lock holder also pushes new frames onto the same head. Two of those at once (owner's store-back against a lock holder's push or store-back) overwrite a list and its frames stay in flight forever, allocatable by nobody. So every store-back is a CAS merge: link the remainder's tail to the head seen, CAS the head to the remainder's head, retry on failure; or the owner takes the lock for its store-back (it is idle, the lock is cheap). ABA is harmless here: the tail links to the head node, not through it, so whatever that node's own link is now, the chain stays whole. A checked build audits in-flight frames: each in exactly one pending list, one done list, or being zeroed by one hart, so a lost list is a stopped boot, not a leak.
> 
> The payer-table decrement for a frame another hart zeroed is by count, payer unknown per frame; the page says the split among entries is by counts, so the reader does not take it for per-frame attribution. Otherwise as the orchestrator wrote: the one-frame wait reason and the unbilled decrement on the page; gates, high-water and longest-in-flight numbers, and the nobody-share trace before the report.

### Implementer · Answer

Event: `8743c51e8dd512d449b1dcbd233323f9` · 2026-10-09T22:35:41Z

> SMP6, on the store-back condition: I took a form that removes store-backs entirely. A pending list is now read and written only under the lock. An idle hart, still holding the lock, cuts up to 64 frames off the front of its list into a private batch (a shared count only), releases the lock, and zeroes and pushes each to done. pop_pending pops under the lock with no swap. So nothing outside the lock writes a pending head, and nothing can merge or be lost.
> The checked build counts every frame in flight against the ownership table at each destruction's audit: pending, staged, done, committing and batch counts. A batch frame is counted done before it leaves its batch, so the check allows the in-motion window and nothing more, and each walk is bounded, so a cycle stops the boot.
> The page states the one-frame wait (only when every frame in flight is in a batch, which pushes per frame) and the by-count, unbilled decrement. Head c37bc477d; measurements, prebuild and sweeps running.

Event: `d410062f3011cb1f0f9b77c9664bdf34` · 2026-10-10T00:09:23Z

> Reopening, blocking for smp6-implementer-2. c37bc477d with (A) passes containment on both widths (R10, deadline_notice met), but sweeps regress vs main: map-anon-search-bound at 2 harts both widths (middle-page search 406 us vs 116; every-page-table 12+ ms vs 10.3, bound 12); sched-cluster-old-control rv32 at 1 and 2 harts (a driver wake misses by 31 ms); sched-lock-contention-4-mttcg rv32 (real time, rerunning). Cause: under icount the harts share one virtual clock, so an idle hart that zeroes instead of halting slows the busy hart's virtual time by up to half; at 1 hart a 64-frame batch with interrupts off delays every wake behind it up to 2 ms, compounding along a chain. Proposed: (A1) an idle hart checks for a pending interrupt after each frame and stops; the batch's rest stays its own for the next idle pass (count/lock rules unchanged): a wake waits one frame (~30 us). (A3) an idle hart zeroes only when every started hart is idle, else it halts; under load frames go on demand at allocation (main's cost). Implementer recommends A1+A3. My view: A1 on its merits, yes. A3 bends the design to the bench: the 2-hart slowdown is icount's shared clock, not a cost real harts see (LAT4 judged the 4-hart tail under MTTCG for this reason), and A3 forgoes parallel zeroing whenever any hart is busy. Alternatives: (A3') keep idle zeroing and judge the icount-sensitive cases net of another hart's idle `z` work, or under MTTCG as LAT4; or accept A3 now as 'no worse than main' with the parallel drain a recorded residual until the bench can judge it. Also: smp-inflight-race reports 'nothing raced' at 1 GiB; it moves to memory pressure (~88-96 MiB), which exercises on-demand zeroing in a case for the first time. Please rule.
